items.title: 大陆深处岩石为何会断裂并下沉？
items.title_orig: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
items.summary: 在一些山脉和火山弧下方，地壳底部的致密岩石会失稳、断裂并下沉数百公里，拖拽岩石圈部分下移。
items.summary_orig: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it.

items.summary_orig: Short answer: give every avatar upload a unique object key, verify the new object, atomically move the user's database pointer, and delete the former object later. items.summary_orig: Your next gaming monitor should be an OLED display. There, I've said it. And I know the notion won't please everyone. items.summary_orig: TL;DR: Generate a short-lived presigned URL on your server, send only that URL to the worker or browser, then upload the image with an HTTP PUT . The access key stays server-side. items.title: 神经网络为何自信却出错，以及如何校准
items.title_orig: Calibration: Why Neural Networks Are Confident and Wrong - and How to Fix Them
items.summary: 校准良好的分类器说 90% 确信就应约 90% 正确，但现代神经网络常严重偏离这一标准。
items.summary_orig: A classifier that says it is 90% sure should be right about 90% of the time. That sounds like a low bar, and yet most modern neural networks fail it badly. They are routinely 99% confident and wrong, or 60% confident and right almost every time. Their accuracy can be excellent while their confidence is meaningless.

items.title: 如何证明 AI 转换的 COBOL 程序的行为仍然相同
items.title_orig: How to prove an AI-converted COBOL program still behaves the same
items.summary: AI 可以将 COBOL 程序转换为 Java，在第一次尝试时编译。干净的编译会告诉您语法是有效的。它没有说明 Java 是否产生与 COBOL 相同的数字，在金融代码中，数字就是整个工作。
items.summary_orig: AI can turn a COBOL program into Java that compiles on the first try. A clean compile tells you the syntax is valid. It says nothing about whether the Java produces the same numbers as the COBOL, and in financial code the numbers are the whole job.

items.summary_orig: TESS watched an exoplanet about 1,000 light years away as it repeatedly transited in front of its star for seven years. But astronomers were surprised to find that the hot Jupiter disappeared. Of course, planets don't just disappear. Something interrupted its transits from our point of view, and astronomers think they've figured out what happened.
